1. Read the question carefully — it names the actual task (a file, a hook, a symptom).
2. Read only the relevant KB files first; if they lack the detail you need, read the actual
   source (`MtgCardImageShapeUtil.tsx`, and if the question touches tldraw's own behavior, its
   source under `node_modules/tldraw/src/lib/tools/SelectTool/childStates/` — don't guess about
   tldraw internals, read them).
3. Answer the specific question — don't dump the whole KB.
4. Flag relevant watch points from `interactions.md`, especially watch point 1 (any ShapeUtil
   defining `onClick` inherits the selection-deferral quirk and needs the matching
   `setSelectedShapes([])` cleanup).
5. Note any knowledge gaps you find while answering — this owner is new and thin; gaps are
   expected and worth recording back via `-update`.

If the question is really about what image/face a card shows rather than how it responds to
clicks/drags, say so and point to `two-faced-cards` instead — see `architecture.md`'s "How to
tell this owner's territory from `two-faced-cards`'s."


ARGUMENTS: Implementing ticket 12 "the library portal" (.scratch/tabletop-cards-come-and-go/issues/12-the-library-portal.md): a new swallow gesture on MtgCardShapeUtil. On drop over the player's own library zone (pointer-keyed via editor.inputs.currentPagePoint, gated to mtg-card shapes and card.props.owner === zone's seatId, following the same pattern as the command-zone gate in zoneHitTest.ts), the card spins twice while shrinking/fading into the library center over ~500ms (needs getInterpolatedProps override since w/h isn't natively interpolated), then the shape is deleted from the store after a POST to Spine succeeds (send-then-commit via sendCardReturnedToSpineBestEffort). Attachments (counters) must fall off via the existing evictPassengers/NON_BATTLEFIELD_ZONES mechanism in cardZoneEntry.ts (library is already in that set). Must work for single card and whole multi-selection dropped together, must not synchronously delete sibling moving shapes during onTranslateEnd (must defer even self-deletion past settle), and the arming swirl renders in viewport space via InFrontOfTheCanvas layer. What do I need to know before planning this?

content.content: 1 --- 2 name: tabletop-shape-mechanics 3 kind: capability 4 --- 5 6 # Tabletop Shape Mechanics 7 8 **The charge**: every gesture on a Tabletop card — tap, drag, drop — must act on the shape 9 actually under the pointer, using tldraw's own selection/translation state machine correctly, 10 even where that state machine has surprising edge cases around custom `ShapeUtil` hooks. This 11 holds regardless of what a shape displays (card face, furniture, future shape types); it's about 12 the *mechanics* of clicking and dragging things on the canvas, not what they look like. 13 14 This capability isn't user-visible as a feature — a player just expects "the card I dragged is 15 the card that moves." But when it breaks, it's a *glaring* bug (see `history.md`, `959831c`): 16 drag one card, then drag another, and the wrong one moves. That's the kind of failure this owner 17 exists to prevent from recurring, and to catch when someone else's change reopens it. 18 19 ## Why this owner exists 20 21 Born 2026-08-07 out of a bug fix (`959831c`, "drag picks up the wrong card after a previous 22 drag"). The finding — a genuine tldraw quirk in its `SelectTool` state machine — initially landed 23 in `owners/two-faced-cards/` purely because that owner's trigger was broad enough to match "the 24 Tabletop's card rendering." It has nothing to do with card faces, flip, or `CardDefinition`. Jess 25 called out that shape-selection mechanics is complex enough to deserve its own standing owner, so 26 future bugs in this territory route here instead of being caught incidentally by a 27 card-rendering owner. See `history.md` for the full migration note. 28 29 ## Scope 30 31 Everything under `apps/tabletop/src/client/shapes/` — `MtgCardShapeUtil.tsx`, 32 `MtgZoneShapeUtil.tsx`, `MtgCounterShapeUtil.tsx`, `MtgCounterTool.ts`, plus the pure seams 33 `zoneHitTest.ts` and `openSpotNearZoneEdge.ts` — and their interaction with tldraw's own 34 `SelectTool` child states (`PointingShape`, `Translating`, in 35 `node_modules/tldraw/src/lib/tools/SelectTool/childStates/`). 36 Concretely: click/tap toggling, drag-and-drop (including drag-and-drop *parenting* — counters 37 attaching to cards), shape selection state, zone detection via shape bounds, custom creation 38 tools, and any tldraw quirk discovered while implementing these. 39 40 **Ticket 02/12** (`.scratch/tabletop-physics/issues/12-*.md`, landed 2026-08-08) carried out the 41 rewrite decided by ticket 02: the card is now a genuine custom shape type, `mtg-card`, defined in 42 `apps/tabletop/src/shared/mtgCardShape.ts` and rendered by `MtgCardShapeUtil` extending 43 `BaseBoxShapeUtil` (not `ImageShapeUtil`). The old `MtgCardImageShapeUtil.tsx` is deleted. 44 45 **Ticket 13** (`.scratch/tabletop-physics/issues/13-*.md`, landed 2026-08-08) did the same for 46 furniture: the playmat, library, graveyard, exile, and the Stack are now a genuine custom shape 47 type, `mtg-zone`, defined in `apps/tabletop/src/shared/mtgZoneShape.ts` and rendered by 48 `MtgZoneShapeUtil` extending `BaseBoxShapeUtil`. Furniture is **no longer** "stock locked 49 `geo`/`image` shapes with no custom ShapeUtil" — that was true before this ticket, isn't now. 50 `MtgZoneShapeUtil` defines no interaction hooks at all (see `architecture.md`), which makes it 51 the KB's working example of "a locked shape needs none." See `architecture.md` for the mechanics 52 and the tldraw registration gotchas both rewrites surfaced. 53 54 **Ticket 17** (`.scratch/tabletop-physics/issues/17-flip-and-face-down.md`, landed 2026-08-09, 55 `eb24a4f`/`ff5d58a`) added the app's **first custom tldraw `ContextMenu`** — 56 `apps/tabletop/src/client/CardContextMenu.tsx`, wired via `TLComponents.ContextMenu` in 57 `TablePage.tsx` — carrying Flip/Turn face-down/Tap-Untap menu items for `mtg-card`. Mechanics 58 territory here is narrow but real: right-clicking a card selects it exactly like `PointingShape` 59 does, and unlike a locked shape's selection (which tldraw clears when the context menu closes), 60 an **unlocked card's selection survives menu close** — reopening watch point 1's stale-selection 61 hazard through a second gesture besides drag. See `architecture.md`'s "Ticket 17" section and 62 watch point 15. 63 64 **Ticket 18** (`.scratch/tabletop-physics/issues/18-counters.md`, landed 2026-08-08, `4c64ef2`) 65 added a third custom shape type: `mtg-counter`, an **unlocked, draggable, text-editable disc** 66 a player drops onto a card. Attachment is tldraw drag-and-drop *parenting*, mediated by drag 67 hooks on `mtg-card` (`canReceiveNewChildrenOfType`/`onDragShapesIn`/`onDragShapesOut`); a card 68 entering graveyard/exile/library evicts its counters to open spots near the zone's edge. 69 **Naming caution**: table-layout ticket 12's decided-but-unbuilt life counter also used the 70 working name `mtg-counter` — ticket 18 claimed the type string per the tabletop-physics spec, 71 so the life counter is named `mtg-life-counter` instead. The old locked-furniture `mtg-counter` 72 cautions in this KB describe *that* shape, not this one — see `architecture.md`. 73 74 **Ticket 19** (`.scratch/tabletop-physics/issues/19-notes.md`, landed 2026-08-10) generalized 75 ticket 18's counter-hosting into a "passenger" concept (`PASSENGER_TYPES`) and added tldraw's 76 **stock `note` shape** as a second passenger type — the first time this KB's mechanics reach past 77 this app's own custom shape types into a stock one tldraw ships. Notes attach to cards via the 78 same parenting mechanism counters use, and ride/detach/evict identically. ## What I found before planning ticket 12

**Read**: this owner's full KB (`README.md`, `architecture.md`, `interactions.md`, `history.md`), `cardZoneEntry.ts`, `sendCardReturned.ts`, `mtgCardShape.ts`, `card.returned.v1.json`, `cardArrival.ts`, and grepped the client/server for existing wiring. Two things this KB has **no** coverage of yet (`getInterpolatedProps`, `InFrontOfTheCanvas`) and I couldn't read tldraw's source to fill the gap — **this worktree has no `node_modules` installed at all** (`apps/tabletop/node_modules` doesn't exist). Run `npm install` from the repo root before planning the animation/arming-layer mechanics; this KB's own philosophy is "read tldraw source, don't guess," and right now you can't.

### Patterns to reuse, not reinvent

- **Arming should mirror `zoneHitTest.ts`'s `armedZoneIdSignal`/`useIsZoneArmed`** — pointer-keyed via `editor.inputs.currentPagePoint` + `editor.isIn("select.translating")`, one shared `computed()` per `Editor` in a `WeakMap`, not per-zone. The library-portal swirl is new *rendering location* (viewport space via tldraw's `InFrontOfTheCanvas` component override, not inside `MtgZoneShapeUtil.component()`), but the *signal* should be the same one, extended, not a parallel implementation.
- **Ownership gate: copy the command-zone pattern exactly** (`interactions.md` watch point 19). `allDraggedCardsAreOwnersCommander(editor, seatId)` in `zoneHitTest.ts` is the template — filter `editor.getSelectedShapes()` to `mtg-card`, require every one to satisfy `props.owner === hit.seatId`. Ticket 12 doesn't need the `isCommander` half. Watch point 9's already-settled rule ("one destination for the whole group, or none") applies directly: a partial-ownership multi-select should not arm/swallow at all, same posture as command zones.
- **Eviction is already free.** `cardZoneEntry.ts`'s `NON_BATTLEFIELD_ZONES` already includes `"library"`, and `evictPassengers` already fires on library entry inside `handleTranslateEnd`. No new plumbing needed for counters/notes falling off — just don't accidentally bypass `handleTranslateEnd`'s existing branch when adding the swallow.

### Real gaps / decisions this ticket has to make, not inherited from an existing pattern

1. **Pointer-keyed drop vs. per-shape zone detection are two different mechanisms today, and ticket 12 asks for the former.** `handleTranslateEnd`'s `zoneAt()` resolves each moved shape's *own* settled bounds center against `topmostZoneAt` — called once per shape in a multi-select, each independently. But the ticket explicitly wants "pointer-keyed... for a single card and a multi-selection alike" (the same design watch point 9 already forced for arming, and for the same reason — a rigid group has one destination). You'll need to decide: does the swallow decision read `editor.inputs.currentPagePoint` instead of each shape's own bounds, and then treat *every currently selected `mtg-card`* as swallowed, independent of what `handleTranslateEnd` computes per-shape? If so, the per-shape `onTranslateEnd` call for a passenger member of the selection needs to know "am I part of a group whose pointer-drop landed on my own library" rather than trusting its own `zoneAt()` result — a real design decision, not a lookup.

2. **`onTranslateEnd` must never synchronously delete a sibling still-settling shape, and must defer even self-deletion past settle** (ticket text, confirmed nowhere else in the KB — this is new). The existing hook always returns a `TLShapePartial` synchronously (prop/meta writes only) or `undefined`. Deletion has to happen later — after the ~500ms shrink/spin/fade animation *and* after the Spine POST resolves (send-then-commit). That means: return a synchronous partial as usual from `onTranslateEnd` (to keep tldraw's per-shape settle contract intact), kick off `editor.animateShapes` + the POST as an async side effect, and call `editor.deleteShapes` only once both finish — not from inside the hook's synchronous return path. Watch point 14's warning ("never swap `queueMicrotask` for `setTimeout`, a macrotask can interleave with input events") is about a different mechanism (multi-untap's undo coalescing) but is a relevant caution for whatever deferral primitive you pick here too.

3. **`getInterpolatedProps` is undocumented in this KB and I could not confirm its signature from tldraw source** (no `node_modules`). Ticket text says it's needed because `w`/`h` aren't natively interpolated by tldraw's shape animation (only x/y/rotation/opacity are, confirmed in `architecture.md`'s "Stack landing collision avoidance" and multiple other sections — nothing there mentions a `w`/`h` interpolation override existing anywhere in this codebase; this would be the first). Get `node_modules` installed and read `ShapeUtil.ts`'s `getInterpolatedProps` before committing to a signature.

4. **`InFrontOfTheCanvas` is a brand-new territory for this app** — no existing custom `TLComponents` entry for it (`TablePage.tsx` currently overrides `ContextMenu`/`Toolbar` only, per `files.md`). You're adding a new component-override slot, the same category of thing `CardContextMenu.tsx` did for `ContextMenu` — expect the same category of "is this component overridable via `TLComponents`" question that watch point 26's `MenuClickCapture` finding warns is *not* always true. Verify `InFrontOfTheCanvas` is actually swappable before designing around it.

5. **`gameCardIndex` is not on `MtgCardShapeProps` at all**, and `sendCardReturnedToSpineBestEffort`'s `CardReturnedParams.gameCardIndex` is *required* (matching `card.returned.v1`'s required field). `card.played`'s payload carries `gameCardIndex?: number` (optional) but `cardArrival.ts`/`mtgCardShape()` never store it into the shape's props — it's dropped today. You'll need to add it to `MtgCardShapeProps` (watch point 16: edit `mtgCardShape()` in `tableFurniture.ts`, the single canonical mint site, not each call site) before the client can ever include it in a swallow request. Also decide what happens for a card with no `gameCardIndex` (e.g. a commander/ghost minted by `seatJoined.ts`, which doesn't carry one) — the contract requires the field.

6. **`sendCardReturnedToSpineBestEffort` is server-side only** (imports `node:crypto`, lives in `src/server/`) and **has zero callers anywhere in the codebase right now** — it and its test were built ahead of this ticket, evidently for exactly this purpose, but the wiring gap is unfilled. There is currently **no client→Tabletop-server HTTP route for any card action** — every existing `mtg-card` mutation is a pure tldraw store write via ShapeUtil hooks; `server.ts`'s only POST route is `seat.joined`. `playerName` and the Spine's real `tableId` are known server-side (per-room state in `rooms.ts`) but **not available to the browser client** at all today. So this ticket needs a new server route (client `fetch` → new `POST` endpoint on the Tabletop's own Express server → `sendCardReturnedToSpineBestEffort`) — this is new architecture for the app, not a gap-fill of an existing seam, and is worth a deliberate design decision (route shape, what the client sends vs. what the server looks up) rather than backing into it.

### Suggested next step
Given the scope of gap #6 especially (new client→server HTTP surface, first of its kind on this ship), and the missing `node_modules` blocking gaps #3/#4, I'd get `npm install` running first, then plan the shape-identity change (`gameCardIndex` prop) and the new server route as their own sub-steps before touching the ShapeUtil hook itself. Happy to consult `two-faced-cards` briefly too if the swallow needs to reset `face`/`faceDown` on the way out (existing `resetFace` logic in `handleTranslateEnd` already does this for ordinary library entry) — flagging that as a likely small interaction, not investigated further here since it's outside this owner's territory.
